chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyaba, who said:

Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) gave me one thousand gold coins and ordered me to distribute them among the families of those who were killed alongside Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him). So I distributed them, and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, the brother of Fudayl al-Rassan, received four gold coins.

key_terms.أصيب: Was struck down, killed — in this context, martyred in battle
key_terms.دفع: Gave, handed over — implies a deliberate, authoritative act of giving
key_terms.دينار: Gold coin (dinar), the standard gold currency of the Islamic world
key_terms.عيال: Dependents, family members — those who depended on the slain for livelihood

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq support the families of those who fought with Zayd ibn Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) entrusted Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyaba with one thousand dinars to distribute to the families of those who had been killed fighting alongside Zayd ibn Ali (AS) in his uprising against the Umayyads in 122 AH. This demonstrates the Imam's practical concern for the welfare of the martyrs' families and his tacit approval of Zayd's revolt, even though the Imam himself did not participate in it.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from `Abd al-Rahman b. Siyaba. He said:

Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) gave me one thousand gold coins, and he ordered me to distribute it to the families who lost members with Zayd b. `Ali (as). So, I distributed it. I gave `Abdullah b. al-Zubayr the brother of Fudayl al-Rassan four gold coins.
